thread_title: Sarracenia 'Adrian Slack' Santa Rosa Co, FL
breadcrumb: Sarracenia 'Adrian Slack' Santa Rosa Co, FL

posts.body_html:
My Adrian slack this fall. It just produced a pitcher one week ago. It's already colorful like that. I received it this summer, bare roots, pitchers all cut off, so basically just a rhizome and roots. I potted it and it produced a very small pitcher in august, then it produced this large one.

Since Adrian Slack is very notorious for being slow to start and color up, I potted it and put it in my grow tent under strong artificial light. So if you are wondering what Adrian Slack looks like under artificial light, there it is. I am sure if I had just potted it and put it outside, it would be as dull as can be after being shipped bare roots like that. Not even sure it would have pitchers, at least probably very dull. This pic is straight out of my iphone, no post processing of any kind. It's really like that.

posts.body_html:
Last winter my adrian slack rotted due to weather switching from spring like weather to sub zero every other week, forcing me to chop it into 6 pieces. I changed its potting media from long fiber sphagnum to peat and perlite, and had 0 expectations that it would look at all decent this season.

It didn't even look like it would when it started growing, being totally green with a reddish throat.

Here it is in all of it's green glory in early May.


But by no means did I expect it to look remotely as nice as it does now.
Four of a kind!

It's not as good looking as last year, though I'm not complaining, since it's one of the better looking plants right now because of the terrible season I've had so far, with over 10 plants rotting, forcing me to cut them up or toss them.
It's still one of my more vigorous plants despite being chopped to pieces this season too.

posts.body_html:
some super old photographs of S. Adrian Slack greenhouse grown (at CC's!) This clone looks so different depending on where it's grown.

I was having a conversation with a grower today about his Adrian slack sulking in his cooler, pacific northwest conditions, and one thing that I've also noticed is that this clone likes heat! One way to grow these in cooler climates is to not sit them in large volumes of water: that water cools down at night, and since it has a high heat capacity, that water can stay cool throughout the day, keeping the soil below optimal temperature ranges. Instead, only put enough water in the tray so that the peat stays hydrated at all times, but never sits in water. When it's sunny, even if it's cool outside, the peat will heat up and so will the soil: this is how I get away with growing them here in my climate where the air temperature is several degrees below optimal.

Anyways, the pics! These were taken July 27, 2013:

posts.body_html:
Elaine (my wife) was helping me weed the other day and she said "oh wow, this one is nice!" Usually, I'm bringing plants to her and asking if they're cute, and her response is almost guaranteed a thumbs down....so when I heard her say that Adrian slack was looking good, it either means the world is ending soon or she genuinely likes it, which is more rare than any of the endangered Sarracenia.

Here's what she saw:
